finding.claim: When the scheduler webhook is enabled but no token is configured, the token check is skipped and any unauthenticated POST can trigger scheduled jobs, including forcing a specific job via ?job=.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to the scheduler webhook route; no Authorization header yields $token = null (SchedulerController.php:86-91); ?job= query parameter (SchedulerController.php:94-95).
finding.sink: Scheduler::processWebhookTrigger runs jobs: $job->inForeground()->run() for ?job= (Scheduler.php:1100-1104), otherwise all due jobs.

trace.note: Only the scheduler.modern.webhook.enabled toggle is checked here.
Authorization header read; absent header leaves $token null.
Null token and jobId passed to processWebhookTrigger.
webhookToken loaded from modernConfig webhook.token, which defaults to null (system/config/scheduler.yaml:35).
if ($this->webhookToken && $token !== $this->webhookToken): with webhookToken null the whole check is skipped (fail open).
?job= selects a job by id and runs it in the foreground.

finding.guards_checked: Webhook enabled flag (SchedulerController.php:81, Scheduler.php:1087) is the only gate that passes. Plugin gate isWebhookEnabled() (Scheduler.php:627-633) is not applied by the controller. Not verified: whether the admin blueprint refuses to enable webhooks without a token, and whether route registration (in the scheduler-webhook plugin, not in this repo) enforces the plugin gate. Impact is running admin-defined jobs out of schedule, not arbitrary command injection; no path from request into the job command string was found.

finding.claim: The webhook bearer token is compared with !== instead of a constant-time comparison.

trace.note: Bearer token extracted from Authorization header.

finding.guards_checked: Token must be non-empty to be compared (see webhook-empty-token-fail-open). Exploitation over a network is impractical; hardening fix is hash_equals.

finding.claim: CSRF nonce verification uses === against the expected MD5 nonce rather than a constant-time comparison.
finding.source: Nonce value supplied with a request to verifyNonce.
finding.sink: Nonce equality check in Utils::verifyNonce (Utils.php:1515 and :1520).

trace.note: verifyNonce receives the request nonce; arrays reduced to first element.
Nonce string built from tick, action, username, session_id and Security::getNonceKey().
Nonce key is 32 random bytes (64 hex chars) stored in a private file.

finding.guards_checked: Nonce is MD5 over a 256-bit server secret, session id, username and time tick, so recovering it via timing is not practical. Hardening only; use hash_equals.

finding.claim: Legacy plaintext password stored in user YAML is compared with !==, which is not constant-time.
finding.source: Plaintext password submitted at login, passed to authenticate().
finding.sink: Equality check against the stored plaintext password at UserTrait.php:54.

trace.note: hashed_password read; Authentication::verify still runs for timing.
Plaintext password field read when present.
Non-constant-time !== comparison; mismatch returns false, match forces a hash upgrade.

finding.guards_checked: Only applies to accounts still carrying a plaintext password field. The hash verify still runs. Low severity; hash_equals would close it.
